prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a hit while turning left. Plain text. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1193; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant, subject to and without waiving its right to contest coverage, responds to Plaintiff's Original Petition as follows. Pursuant to Rule 92 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure, Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the credible evidence.

For its first affirmative defense, Defendant asserts comparative responsibility. Plaintiff's own negligence, including failure to keep a proper lookout, failure to yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic, and failure to maintain a safe speed under the circumstances, proximately caused or contributed to the collision. Any recovery must be reduced in proportion to Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code.

For its second affirmative defense, Defendant asserts sole proximate cause. The conduct of a third party, over whom Defendant had no control, was the sole proximate cause of the occurrence and of Plaintiff's alleged injuries.

For its third affirmative defense, Defendant asserts failure to mitigate damages. Plaintiff failed to exercise reasonable care to mitigate any alleged damages, including by failing to follow prescribed medical treatment, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.
